summary.text: Russ Miner is a Republican state representative from Montana who has represented House District 26 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A Great Falls native with a career in agriculture consulting, he has served on the House Natural Resources and Taxation committees and is vice chair of the Agriculture Committee.

paragraphs.text: Russ Miner was born in Great Falls, Montana, where he lives, and graduated from C.M. Russell High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree in agricultural production operations from Montana State University-Bozeman in 1976.
His career experience includes owning an agricultural consulting business and working as a fertilizer director and manager at the Wilbur-Ellis company.
Miner began serving as a board member of the Cascade County Farm Bureau Federation in 2018.
Miner won the House general election in 2022 and was re-elected on November 5, 2024.
In the 2025-2026 session he is assigned to the House Natural Resources and House Taxation committees and is vice chair of the Agriculture Committee.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, Miner said he is seeking a third term representing a district that covers part of Cascade County and all of Chouteau County, and that he serves on the Water Policy Interim Committee.

He listed his key campaign messages as protecting senior water rights and exempt wells, placing limits on data centers covering water use, energy costs, noise, light and share of property taxes, and reforming property taxes.
